samples.summary: `--raw`'s stated contract ("so `sheets import` round-trips formulas") does not hold at the import call site the diff never touched
samples.evidence: The new `--raw` flag exists only to make an export→import round trip preserve formulas (`packages/cli/src/commands/sheets-export.ts:31-34`, `packages/cli/skills/sheets-import-export.md:104-107`, `packages/cli/skills/recipe-csv-pipeline.md:47-51`, `scripts/agent/charters/round-trip.md:15`). The importer it names cannot do that: `buildCellMap` (packages/cli/src/util/csv-parse.ts:93) emits `cells[ref] = { value }` and never a `formula`, and the backend keeps them as distinct fields — `packages/backend/src/api/v1/cells.controller.ts:123` writes `f: body.formula ?? existing?.f`, so a value of `=SUM(B2:B100)` is stored as text, not a formula, with or without `--raw`. Worse, `sheets export` serializes the `getCells` response, which is a list of `{ ref, value, formula }` records (see the fixture in packages/cli/test/sheets-export.test.ts:59-62), so the CSV is a three-column table with a `ref,value,formula` header, not a cell grid; re-importing it lands the literal strings `ref`/`value`/`formula` and `E2`/`E3` into A1:C3. The consequence is that users and agents following the skill docs pass `--raw` — switching off the new CSV-injection guard — in exchange for a round trip that does not work. Fix belongs either on the docs/flag rationale or on `sheets-import` (map a `formula` column onto the `formula` field).

samples.summary: Design-doc command synopsis for `sheets export` still describes the pre-`--raw` option set
samples.evidence: docs/design/cli.md:366-367 lists `export <doc-id> <file> [--tab] [--range] [--file-format csv|json]` with no `--raw`, while §8.1 of the same file (docs/design/cli.md:919-923) and `packages/cli/src/schema/registry.ts:576` both document the flag. The synopsis is the part a reader scans for available flags, so it is left describing the old contract.

samples.summary: The formula guard was wired into `format()` for every `--format csv` consumer, but only `sheets export` was given an opt-out
samples.evidence: `format(data,'csv')` now always passes `{ neutralizeFormulas: true }` (packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:61), which changes the bytes emitted by every other `output()` caller — e.g. the documented pipe example `wafflebase --format csv sheets cells get abc-123 A1:B3` (packages/documentation/developers/cli.md:632) and `wafflebase sheets cells get ... --format csv` used as machine input. Those consumers have no `--raw` equivalent, so a cell whose value starts with `=`/`+`/`-`/`@` silently gains a leading apostrophe in any downstream tool that consumes CLI CSV. `sheets export` (packages/cli/src/commands/sheets-export.ts:63) is the only call site that was given the escape hatch.

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out in the tree. `--raw` is documented as existing so `sheets import` round-trips formulas (packages/cli/src/commands/sheets-export.ts:31-34, :56-59; skills/sheets-import-export.md:104-107; skills/recipe-csv-pipeline.md:47-52,62), but the import path it names cannot preserve formulas: sheets-import.ts:81 calls buildCellMap, which emits only `{ value }` (packages/cli/src/util/csv-parse.ts:87-94), and the backend batch handler stores value and formula as distinct fields (packages/backend/src/api/v1/cells.controller.ts:168-172), so `=SUM(B2:B100)` is persisted as text `v` with `f` unset. No server-side inference exists (inferInput is only in packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/input.ts:229-240; no backend reference). Additionally, `sheets export` serializes the getCells record list ({ref,value,formula,style} — cells.controller.ts:60-65) through formatCsv, which emits an object-key header row plus one line per record (packages/cli/src/output/csv.ts:84,98-101; fixture at packages/cli/test/sheets-export.test.ts:56-62), so the exported CSV is a records table, not a cell grid, and re-importing it writes the literal `ref/value/formula` header and `E2`/`E3` strings into A1:C3. Net effect: users and agents are steered to switch off the CSV-injection guard for a round trip that does not work — a contract asserted against consumers (csv-parse.ts, sheets-import.ts, the backend) the diff never updated, which is exactly this lens's lane and reachable on the documented path. No guard or transformation elsewhere rescues it, so there is no ground to refute.

finding.summary: Browser login now dead-ends on a raw backend 400 when the OAuth state cookie is gone; the frontend consumer has no error path
finding.evidence: The frontend's only OAuth entry point is `packages/frontend/src/components/login-form.tsx:27` (`<Link to={VITE_BACKEND_API_URL}/auth/github>`), and `packages/frontend/src/app/login/page.tsx` (whole file) has no handling for a failed callback — there is no `?error=` route and no other consumer of the callback. Previously `GET /auth/github/callback` always ended in `res.redirect(FRONTEND_URL)`; it now throws `BadRequestException` (packages/backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts:131-150) whenever `wafflebase_oauth_state` is absent or mismatched. Reachable without any attacker: the cookie's `STATE_COOKIE_MAX_AGE_MS` is 10 minutes (packages/backend/src/auth/oauth-state.ts), shorter than a first-time GitHub signup/2FA leg; and because the cookie is set at a fixed name/path on every `/auth/github` visit, a second login tab overwrites the first tab's secret, so the earlier tab's callback also 400s. The user lands on the backend origin looking at raw Nest JSON with no way back. Fix belongs either on the new callback code (redirect to `FRONTEND_URL` with an error query instead of throwing) or on the frontend login page.

verdict.reason: Both halves of the presence claim are false in this tree. (1) The callback does not throw BadRequestException for a missing/mismatched OAuth state cookie: auth.controller.ts:144-146 and :157-159 both `return res.redirect(this.loginErrorUrl('oauth_state'))`, and loginErrorUrl at :270-274 builds `${FRONTEND_URL}/login?error=oauth_state` on the frontend origin. The only remaining BadRequestExceptions on that handler are :166 (invalid CLI port) and :183 (expired CLI state), which are the CLI branch, not the browser-cookie case. (2) The frontend does have an error path: app/login/page.tsx:15,49 reads `?error=` via useSearchParams and passes it to LoginForm; components/login-form.tsx:15-18 maps `oauth_state` to a message, :21 gives a generic fallback for unknown codes, :31-33 resolves it, and :48-55 renders it in a role="alert" block directly above the retry link at :56-74. App.tsx:81 registers the `/login` route the redirect targets. The underlying preconditions (10-min STATE_COOKIE_MAX_AGE_MS at oauth-state.ts:26; fixed cookie name/path at oauth-state.ts:20,65 so a second tab overwrites the first) are real, but they result in the user landing on the frontend login page with an explanation and a working retry, not a raw Nest 400 dead-end. The described broken consumer does not exist.
